page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-16 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores presenting 8 vCPUs via multithreading, alongside 16 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The architecture incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data storage relies on attached network block volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate elevated single-thread efficiency alongside balanced multi-threaded performance. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server scores 3,292.26, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, and achieves a top-tier score of 3,091.0 in Geekbench text processing. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 33.57 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core registers 2,174.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance scales proportionally to core count, yielding 13,310.44 in stress-ng and 8,913.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 72.51 GB/sec read and 49.87 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting static web throughput of 13.88 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 11.96 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the configuration offers dense compute per gigabyte of memory, maximizing core allocation for processing-heavy workloads without excess memory overhead. The lack of bundled local storage introduces network I/O considerations for disk-intensive services. VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-16 is well-suited for compute-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch compression, text processing, and scalable microservices or web serving layers that require strong per-thread execution.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-16 is a compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets, it delivers top-tier single-thread performance, posting 3,292.26 in stress-ng and strong Geekbench single-core scores of 2,174.0. Multi-threaded metrics remain balanced, reaching 13,310.44 in stress-ng and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 72.51 GB/sec. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on external network block storage. Offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM profile, this server provides cost-effective CPU resource density ideal for CI/CD compilation, web serving, text parsing, and batch processing workloads.
